$comment: Ground truth for Fernway (CONTRACT.md, "Planted bugs" and "V2 planted bugs"; V06-V09 are docs/v2-spec.md "Fernway (0.5.0 planned bugs)"). Each bug is enabled with FERNWAY_BUGS=<id> and must be caught by `detectedBy` on `page` (a route; "*" = every route, checked on / by the acceptance suite); `scenario`, when present, names the scenario (of that check) that catches it and `alsoOn` lists other pages it shows on. Pages under /app are tested signed in as Alex (Run Hound account A, with Sam as account B). tests/acceptance/src/fernway.acceptance.test.ts asserts each bug's detectedBy check. Clean mode must give zero confirmed findings.

bugs.title: Waitlist "Team size" select has no accessible name (its label isn't associated)
Newsletter: a failed save is swallowed (catch {}) and nothing is shown
Quick add: "Add task" never disables and the server ignores the Idempotency-Key, so a double click adds 2 tasks
Profile: Bio shows as saved (toast) but the client drops it before sending
Icon-only buttons (sidebar collapse, notifications) have no accessible name
Stripe-style live secret key (sk_live_..., fake) shipped in the JavaScript bundle
Focus ring removed on the sign-up inputs (outline-none, no ring)
No security headers: no Content-Security-Policy, clickjacking protection or nosniff
Session cookie fernway_session is readable by JavaScript (no HttpOnly)
Sign-in errors are red text only: no role="alert", not linked to the fields
GET /api/users/:id/profile returns any user's profile to any signed-in user (no ownership check)
The workspace APIs answer without a session (only the SPA redirects)
PUT /api/users/:id/profile stores any key it is sent, including role and plan (mass assignment)
Opening /app/help directly answers 404 (no SPA fallback for that path; the sidebar links to it)
PATCH /api/tasks/:id updates another user's task (no ownership check on the write)
Writes to /api/tasks/:id work without a session
Session cookie set SameSite=None; Secure, and the task save accepts a form-encoded body with no CSRF token or Origin check
/app/upgraded sets plan: "pro" on load (the server trusts the success page; no payment needed)
